libs.note: BH-5565: Watchman's collector, run by bin/staff.sh tick watchman. It prints two deterministic checks as staff findings: history-secret (a gitleaks location in the git history of a fleet repo on this box; one beat per scan with new locations; the location only, never a value) and rotation-due (a credential in catalog/staff-rotations.d/ past its due date). A rotated credential closes its filed issue as completed and posts outcome merged. Applied by the collector with lib_env_apply staff-watchman. Note: docs/notes/2026-10-15-BH-5565-watchman.md.

knobs.note: The directory that holds the fleet repos on the box that runs the staff lane: <root>/<project>. A project with no repo there is logged once per interval, not scanned. The scan reads the clone as it is and never fetches.

A repo is scanned again when its last attempt is older than this. A leaked key in history is found within a day of the commit reaching the box. Out of range is one warn line in logs/staff.log and the default.

At most this many due repos are scanned per staff tick, oldest attempt first. Each repo runs chunks while the tick budget lasts (STAFF_COLLECT_TIMEOUT_S minus 20 s). A repo whose scan is not done is due again at once, behind the repos that waited longer. Out of range is one warn line in logs/staff.log and the default.

The limit on one gitleaks run. It never goes past the tick budget (STAFF_COLLECT_TIMEOUT_S minus 20 s); a value that does not fit is one warn line and the budget. A chunk of more than one commit that times out halves the chunk size; one commit that times out is a failed scan: nothing saved, and the next due scan repeats the range.

The most commits one gitleaks run reads, oldest first. A repo with more unscanned commits is scanned in chunks with a saved cursor (state/staff/watchman/scan/

.tips), so a large history finishes over several runs and ticks. A timeout halves the chunk for that repo (scan/

.chunk); a run that takes under a quarter of the scan limit doubles it back, up to this value.

A repo's first full scan with at most this many locations files each location as a history-secret finding. More = a baseline: the locations go to state/staff/watchman/base/

.jsonl, ONE history-baseline finding names the count, the files and the top rules, and one beat. Later scans file only locations not in the baseline. 100 is 5 claim windows at STAFF_MAX_ITEMS 20.

The failed scan attempts in a row of one repo (or pinned gitleaks installs that fail) that send ONE warn beat through bin/lane-alert.sh: the repo's history is not covered. A good scan resets the count.

The bin/lane-alert.sh severity of the beat for a scan with new history-secret locations: critical, warn, info or off. off sends no beat; the finding still flows. Any other value is one warn line and critical.
Test seam: a file the collector sources after its libs, only when HARNESS_TEST_SANDBOX=1. NOT settable from the control plane: it names a file a root lane sources.
Test seam: the epoch the collector uses for its windows, due dates and observedAt, only when HARNESS_TEST_SANDBOX=1. NOT settable from the control plane.
Test seam: the path of a gitleaks binary to use instead of the pinned install, only when HARNESS_TEST_SANDBOX=1. NOT settable from the control plane: it names a binary a root lane runs.
Test seam gate: the collector reads WM_FIXTURE, WM_NOW and WM_GITLEAKS only when this is 1. Never set on a box, and NOT settable from the control plane.
